_about: Provenance for ping fixtures. Files under 'captured' are real /localapi/v0/ping replies from one standalone Tailscale daemon, sanitized; their bytes match 'sha256'. Files under 'synthetic' were written by hand and are not captures. Capturing from 1.102.2 does not add it to the tested daemon-version matrix in LocalAPI/manifest.json.

ping-captured-disco-direct.json.capture_command: spike tool that Scripts/capture-ping-fixture.py was adapted from (same request and sanitization rules)

ping-captured-icmp.json.capture_command: spike tool that Scripts/capture-ping-fixture.py was adapted from (same request and sanitization rules)

ping-captured-peerapi.json.capture_command: spike tool that Scripts/capture-ping-fixture.py was adapted from (same request and sanitization rules)

ping-captured-tsmp.json.capture_command: spike tool that Scripts/capture-ping-fixture.py was adapted from (same request and sanitization rules)

sanitization: Tailscale IPv4/IPv6 of this node, the target peer, and the offline peer -> 100.64.0.1-3 / fd7a:115c:a1e0::1-3
host names -> example-self, example-peer, example-offline-peer; MagicDNS FQDN -> example-peer.example.ts.net. (trailing dot kept)
RFC 1918 endpoint address -> 192.0.2.N; public IPv4 -> 203.0.113.N; global IPv6 -> 2001:db8::N (brackets and port kept)
ports, region IDs and codes, latencies, error strings, key names, key order, and JSON value types unchanged

synthetic.ping-derp-sample.json: hand-written DERP reply; no DERP reply has been captured
synthetic.ping-error-sample.json: hand-written error reply; the error string is illustrative
synthetic.ping-sample.json: hand-written direct disco reply; omits Err and PeerRelay, which real replies always carry
